roles.name: pk-metal-admin
roles.description:
What the platform admins need: every pk-metal kind, and the Secrets and ConfigMaps of the operator's namespace (the Role below). Bind both to the admin group, the group that the admission policies name (ConfigMap hostoperation-approval, key adminGroup, default pk-metal:admins); the sample site overlay does (config/samples/site-overlay/bindings.yaml).

What it leaves out on purpose: - impersonate, escalate, bind and the RBAC objects. An admin who can act as another user can approve in the name of an approver, or lift a guard in the name of another person, and the record names the wrong person. cluster-admin has all three; - the status of the kinds: the operator writes it, and it says what the operator found. A member can still get a token of the operator with create on Secrets in pk-metal: see the threat model of the docs site; - Secrets outside the operator's namespace; - CRDs, admission policies and the manager's Deployment. Installing and upgrading the operator, and pk-metal pivot, are cluster-admin work.

Edit the list of kinds with the CRDs (a test in internal/envtest checks it).

roles.name: pk-metal-admin
roles.description: The operator's namespace: the BMC logins, the secrets bundles, the published admin credentials, the site settings, the ledger and the Talos config patches. Read access to these Secrets is admin on each managed cluster and each BMC: bind this Role to the admin group only. The logs of the manager and of the imager Jobs are here too.

roles.name: pk-metal-approver
roles.description:
The human side of the approval gate. An operation's target and actions are frozen at creation, so a patch cannot change what an operation does; it sets the approval, and the admission policy checks that an approver signs with their own name. Permission to patch IS permission to approve. A patch can also set annotations: abort, retry, and the guard overrides (override-cluster-guard, ignore-window), which let an approved operation run past the etcd quorum guard or outside a maintenance window. So this role also decides who may lift those guards. Bind it to the people (or the group) who may let a disruptive operation run. Nothing binds it by default, and the manager's own role has no patch on operations.

The same holds for a TalosRollout: what it changes, on which nodes, is frozen at creation and its plan is the operator's status, so a patch approves it, pauses or resumes it, or aborts it. One approval there covers every node's operation of the plan.

It reads what the plan of pk-metal approve names: the Host, its BMC endpoints (whether anybody checks the BMC's certificate), the boot assets (what the BMC mounts), and the clusters and nodes. A plan that the approver cannot read in full says so.

roles.name: pk-metal-backup
roles.description: Reading the etcd backup catalogue and asking for a snapshot now (pk-metal backup now|list). Taking a snapshot reads etcd and changes no machine, so this is not part of the approval split; it holds no Secret and cannot decrypt a backup, which only the holders of the age identities can. Restoring one goes through an approved etcdRecover operation (docs site: operate/day-2/restore-etcd). Bind it to the people who look after backups. Nothing binds it by default.

roles.name: pk-metal-oncall
roles.description: What a person on call needs to follow the runbooks (docs site: operate/runbooks), and no more. The runbooks read every pk-metal kind, and they change a few things that start no machine change by themselves: - delete a failed or aborted HostOperation (pk-metal retry); the operator proposes a new one, which waits for approval again; - patch a HostClaim (pk-metal hold, unhold) and a Host (pk-metal wipe, or remove the disk-not-wiped mark); a wipe is still an operation that a person approves. This patch can also set the guard lifts there (allow-self-disruption, wipe-waived, ack-etcd-risk); guard-lift admission makes each one name that person; - patch a TalosCluster to remove the restore-pending mark after a restore; - patch an Asset to correct its ledger facts; - delete a TalosRollout to stop it for good. It may also read the manager's /metrics (the manager asks the API server whether a caller may get that URL), for a look when Prometheus is down, and the admission policies, to find the one PkMetalAdmissionGateDegraded names. The Role below reads the manager's pod, log and Deployment, and the imager Jobs, in pk-metal only: the runbooks read the manager log. It holds no patch on HostOperations or TalosRollouts: that is approval, and belongs to pk-metal-approver. Bind both to a person who must also approve, abort, or resume. It holds no Secret. The base binds nothing; the sample site overlay binds the ClusterRole and the Role to one group (config/samples/site-overlay/bindings.yaml).

bindings.name: pk-metal-manager
bindings.description: Binds the generated roles (role.yaml, from the +kubebuilder:rbac markers on the reconcilers) to the manager's service account. The ClusterRole covers the cluster-scoped kinds and the claims and operations that live in any namespace; the Role covers what stays inside the operator's namespace: Secrets, the leader-election Lease, cert-manager requests.
